data.name: Ulrike
data.gender_notes: Ulrike is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Ulrich, a name of Germanic origin meaning ‘wealth’ or ‘riches’ and ‘ruler’ or ‘power’. The name Ulrike carries the meaning “Wealth and ruler” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Ulrike usually hope their child will grow to embody wealth and ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of inner strength and prosperity.
data.etymology: Ulrike belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wealth and ruler.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ulrike total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

in_hebrew.name: עוּלְרִיקָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עוּלְרִיקָה - שְׁלוֹמִית, שְׁלוֹמִית, נְקִיָּה. שְׁם נָשִׁים, כְּדֶרֶךְ הַבִּרְיָתָה הַבְּרִית הַשְּׁנִיָּה. קָרֶאנָה לְאִשָּׁה נְקִיָּה, שְׁלוֹמִית וְעֹצֶרֶת - כְּנַשִּׁים הַקֹּדֶשׁ בָּרוּךְ הַבָּא.

in_greek.name: Οὐλρίκη
in_greek.long_meaning: Οὐλρίκη - καθαρή, ειρηνική, ευλογία. Ονομαστική feminine, εφ' ηλικίας. Διδασκαλία του Ιησού. Οὐλρίκη: α) κατ' εὐνοιαν: καλός, όσιος.

in_latin.name: Ulrica
in_latin.long_meaning: Ulrica - nobilis, mundus, pacificus. Ulrica est forma feminina nominis Germanici Uolricus, quod significat 'bellator nobilis' vel 'bellator mundus'.

in_english.name: Ulrike
in_english.long_meaning: Ulrike is a Germanic feminine given name that means 'noble' or 'pure'. It is composed of two elements: 'ul' meaning 'noble' and 'ric' meaning 'power'. The name is associated with the Germanic tribe of the Alemanni and is also found in the Old Norse mythology. In the Christian tradition, the name Ulrike signifies purity, peace, and nobility, reflecting the virtues of a Christian woman.

data.cultural_impact: The name Ulrike can be found in many German speaking countries where Ulrich has a long and rich history. Its cultural significance lies in its association with strength, power, and wealth. In medieval times, Ulrich was a popular name among noble families and the church, reflecting the politically and socially influential people who bore the name.
data.spiritual_significance: From a Christian perspective, the name Ulrike can be seen as a reminder of the spiritual wealth and power that comes from God. First Ulrich, meaning ruler of the world, is a name given by God. Second, it also represents the inner riches that come from having a strong faith, purity of heart, and the gifts of the Holy Spirit, making Ulrike a name with deep spiritual significance.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ulrike: Lightwork, dedication to illumination and enlightenment. A beacon of hope and wisdom in the darkness.

historical_references.reference: Ulrike Meinhof was a German journalist and left-wing activist, a key figure in the West German student movement during the 1960s and a founding member of the Red Army Faction (RAF). She was born on June 4, 1934, in Hamburg, Germany. She died by suicide on May 8, 1976.
historical_references.context: Student protests, left-wing activism, Red Army Faction (RAF)

historical_references.reference: Ulrika Eleonora of Sweden, born on September 19, 1688, was the fourth daughter of King Charles XII of Sweden and Queen Ulrika Eleonora of Denmark. She was known for her intelligence, beauty, and strong-willed personality. She was a patron of the arts and sciences and played an influential role in Swedish politics during the late 17th and early 18th centuries.
historical_references.context: Swedish monarchy, patronage of arts and sciences
